Built against [wamsoft/krkrz_dev](https://github.com/wamsoft/krkrz_dev) V2.6.5

- **A glossary of terms marked in the text**: words the story explains are drawn in their own colour, underlined; a click or a tap shows the word's entry without going on, the backlog marks them too, and Extras has a Glossary tab of the words met (`terms.csv`, a translation with its own)
- **Text settings for the player, with a preview**: Config's new Text page picks the message font (the sample adds Noto Serif JP), an outline and a shadow with their colours, and the read text's colour, beside a small window that types sample lines in that look
- **A colour picker**: a wheel and a brightness bar, by mouse, touch, keys or a controller, for any colour setting
- **An outline and a shadow together, and gradient text**: the message text can have both at once, and `[font gradcolor= edgegradcolor= shadowgradcolor= graddir=]` shade the text, its outline and its shadow down the line or along it
- **Message window styles per scene**: `[env msgstyle=]` gives a flashback or another point of view its own window frame and name box, kept by saves and Back, and the player can tint each style on Config; the Character demo's flashback has a sepia window between letterbox bars
- **The game's fonts and text styles in one place**: `fonts.csv` (with each font's licence, which About lists) and one table of named text styles for the screens' own text
- **Face windows for Live2D and VRM characters**, cut from the model as it's drawn, so they blink and talk there too
- **Fixed**: a `[font]` given before a line's text (a colour, a size, a gradient) no longer disappears in a line mode's clear, and a larger word after a size change in the middle of a line no longer breaks in the middle
- kagex-release's `check` lists web file names with `%`, `#` or `?`, which the web engine can't fetch as loose files
- kagex-release 0.22.0 downloads the 0.22.0 engines

The sample game with Live2D (`kagex_sample_live2d_<platform>`, added to this release once it's out) holds Live2D's Cubism Core: by installing or playing it you agree not to copy the Cubism Core out of it, distribute it apart from the game, modify it, or reverse engineer, decompile or disassemble it. It uses sample data owned and copyrighted by Live2D Inc.

Everything in this release is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/blob/0.22.0/CHANGELOG.md).

On Windows the engine needs OpenGL ES: a graphics driver that supports it, or ANGLE's `libEGL.dll` and `libGLESv2.dll` next to `krkrz.exe`.

The macOS app and tools aren't signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks them the first time: open the app from the context menu (Open), or allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security; for the tools, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine kagex-release kagex-lipsync`. The Android APK is signed with a debug key: allow installs from unknown sources, or use `adb install`. The sample's iOS build is for the Simulator; kagex-release signs a game for iPhones and iPads with your own Apple Developer certificate.
